quickSummary: Mitochondria and Plastids are double-membrane, semi-autonomous organelles originating from engulfed prokaryotic endosymbionts (containing circular dsDNA and 70S ribosomes). Mitochondria feature inner membrane Cristae with Cardiolipin and F0-F1 ATP Synthase complexes (Oxysomes), generating ATP via oxidative phosphorylation. Plastids include photosynthetic Chloroplasts (thylakoid grana and RuBisCO-rich stroma), pigment-rich Chromoplasts, and storage Leucoplasts (Amyloplasts, Elaioplasts, Aleuroplasts).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have double membranes, naked circular dsDNA, 70S ribosomes, and divide by binary fission (Endosymbiont theory).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THE ENDOSYMBIONT THEORY (Lynn Margulis)
                      
   Primitive Anaerobic ──[Engulfed Aerobic Proteobacterium]──► MITOCHONDRIA
   Eukaryotic Ancestor ──[Engulfed Photosynthetic Cyanobacterium]──► CHLOROPLASTS
conceptBreakdown.content: Mitochondria and Plastids are energy-transducing organelles that contain their own naked circular double-stranded DNA, 70S ribosomes, and RNA transcripts, dividing independently by binary fission within eukaryotic host cells.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Mitochondria (Altmann / Benda)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Mitochondria (Altmann / Benda)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MITOCHONDRIAL ULTRASTRUCTURE
                         
           Outer Membrane (Porin Channels, Smooth)
             │
           Intermembrane Space ($H^+$ accumulation)
             │
           Inner Membrane (Cardiolipin, Cristae, $F_0\text{-}F_1$ ATP Synthase)
             │
           Matrix (Krebs Enzymes, dsDNA, 70S Ribosomes)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Outer Membrane**: Smooth and highly permeable due to pore-forming **Porins** ($<5,000\text{ Da}$). 
• **Inner Membrane**: Highly impermeable; rich in the unique phospholipid **Cardiolipin** (four fatty acid tails). Folded into tubular/plate-like **Cristae** to maximize surface area.
• **Oxysomes ($F_0\text{-}F_1$ ATP Synthase Complexes)**: The inner membrane houses ETC complexes I–IV and $F_0\text{-}F_1$ ATP Synthase (Complex V). The hydrophobic $F_0$ base forms a transmembrane proton channel; the spherical $F_1$ headpiece in the matrix catalyzes ATP synthesis.
• **Matrix**: Houses soluble Krebs cycle enzymes (*Citrate Synthase, Isocitrate Dehydrogenase; Succinate Dehydrogenase is anchored to inner membrane as Complex II*), circular dsDNA, and 70S ribosomes.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Plastids & Chloroplast Ultrastructure
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Plastids & Chloroplast Ultrastructure
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PLASTID CLASSIFICATIONS
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                                 ▼                                 ▼
CHLOROPLASTS                      CHROMOPLASTS                      LEUCOPLASTS
(Photosynthetic)                  (Pigmented Non-Photosynthetic)   (Non-Pigmented Storage)
├── Chlorophyll *a*, *b*          ├── Carotenoids ($\beta$-Carotene,├── Amyloplasts (Starch)
└── Thylakoid Grana Architecture     Lycopene, Lutein)             ├── Elaioplasts (Lipids/Oils)
                                  └── Red/Orange/Yellow Colors      └── Aleuroplasts (Proteins)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Plastid Functional Classes**:
  1. **Chloroplasts**: Green photosynthetic plastids containing Chlorophyll *a*, *b* and carotenoids.
  2. **Chromoplasts**: Fat-soluble carotenoid pigments ($\beta$-carotene, lycopene, lutein) imparting yellow, orange, and red colors to petals, fruits (*e.g., Tomato*), and roots (*Carrot*).
  3. **Leucoplasts**: Colorless storage plastids:
     - **Amyloplasts**: Store starch (*e.g., Potato tubers*).
     - **Elaioplasts (Lipidoplasts)**: Store oils and fats (*e.g., Castor seeds*).
     - **Aleuroplasts (Proteoplasts)**: Store proteins (*e.g., Maize aleurone layer*).
• **Chloroplast Architecture**:
  - **Thylakoids & Grana**: Disc-shaped membrane sacs stacked into columns called **Grana**, interconnected by unstacked **Stroma Lamellae (Fret Membranes)**. Thylakoid membranes contain PS-I, PS-II, Cytochrome $b_6f$, and ATP synthase.
  - **Stroma Matrix**: Contains dark reaction enzymes, notably **RuBisCO** (the most abundant enzyme on Earth), circular dsDNA, and 70S ribosomes.
